newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bimantara says gains from rupiah falls.
newsitem.headline: Bimantara says gains from rupiah falls.

text.p: Indonesian conglomerate PT Bimantara Citra said on Friday it would mostly gain from the sharp fall in the rupiah against the U.S. dollar.
Director Abdul Kadir said its broadcasting division had no debt in U.S. dollars and "almost zero" debt in rupiah.
He said revenue from the group's telecommunications division was in U.S. dollars, while loans were in a combination of the local and U.S. currencies. He did not give the amount.

"In this sector, with the effect of the currency today, it gives a gain rather than a loss. The revenue is most often in U.S. dollars," he told a briefing at an international conference on the capital market in Jakarta.
Kadir said all revenue from the transporation and automobile divisions was denominated in U.S. dollars, while loans were a combination of rupiah and dollars.
"The only significant effect (of the rupiah fall) is from one company where we just refinanced our rupiah loan in U.S. dollars," he added without giving details.
He said the company's gas pipeline project on Java island had a debt of $380 million, but added that revenue was in U.S. dollars and the company stood to gain.

The PT Trans Javagas Pipeline is the fourth largest such pipeline in the world, stretching 430 km (267 miles) under the sea from the East Java island of Pagerungan Besar to Gresik in east Java. The pipeline carries 300 million cubic feet of gas per day but is still functioning at only 50 percent capacity.
